instructions: Up to 2 days ahead, or for the freezer: stir 1/4 cup warm water, the sugar and the yeast together in a large bowl. Leave it for about 10 minutes, until it's frothy.

Add 1/4 cup warm milk, the yogurt, olive oil, salt and 2 1/2 cups of the flour. Stir, then knead on a lightly floured counter for 8 minutes, until it's soft and springs back. Add the rest of the flour a spoonful at a time only if it sticks.
Return the dough to the bowl, cover and leave it in a warm spot for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Roll each into a rectangle about 4 inches by 2 inches.
Spread 1 tsp of the softened butter down the middle of each rectangle. Fold the sides over to the center and pinch to seal. Twist, then form a ring and tuck the ends under.
Set the rings on parchment-lined trays, cover loosely and let them rise for 45 minutes, until slightly puffed. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F.
Melt the last 1 tsp butter and stir it into 3 tbsp milk. Brush it over the rolls and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for about 20 minutes, until deep golden. Check the bottoms, and slide a second tray underneath if they're browning too fast. Cool on a rack.
Once completely cool, keep the rolls in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze them for up to 2 months.
To serve, warm them in a 350°F oven for 5 minutes, or 10 to 12 minutes from frozen.
advance_prep_notes: bake the rolls up to 2 days ahead, or freeze them for up to 2 months
method_notes: My Cooking Journey leads (5 from 49): a yogurt and olive oil dough, butter spread inside each roll, a milk and butter wash and sesame on top. Natasha's Baking uses a milk and water dough with an oil-and-butter lamination and agrees on the same ring shape and about 20 minutes at a hot oven. The lead's jam filling is left out, and its yeast amount (1/2 tsp on the card, 1 1/2 tsp in the post) is taken from the post. Neither source gave storage times, so those are general bread guidance. The two rises add about 2 hours.
